parts.direction: Hook, drawn (style hook.mustBeDrawnObject). The series line-art humanoid stands at a control lever on a deterministic rail: it moves in perfect lockstep, ticks stamped at its feet, reading 'DETERMINISTIC'. Frame 1 carries motion (hook.opensOnMotion): the humanoid walks its rail before any type lands. On 'completely deterministic' the rail locks with a click (the style's one accent element: the lock). On 'cannot learn' its grip slackens. On 'baseline of chaos' the rail shatters into drifting dots; on 'real world' the humanoid steps off onto uneven ground and keeps walking. heroLeft band; the face plate carries the speaker. Built inside g01 (like 2.1's lower third): Sreeram Nudurupati / AI for the Working Data Engineer / @snudurupati, name display 900 40px, role 500 24px $muted, wipes up 2s in, out at 7.6, on the lower-left band under the rail (face plate is right; nothing spoken is repeated there).
parts.draw: series humanoid; rail; lock; chaos dots

parts.direction: The opening statement as a quote card on the right plate. Small eyebrow 'THE CLAIM' 22px $muted; the quote builds verbatim line by line as spoken, 44px display, '$accent' on 'stochasticity' only (accentElementsPerScene=1). Attribution block lands on 'Dennis Noble': 'Dennis Noble' 900 / 'on biological intelligence, quoting Alan Turing' 500 $muted / '1950' on the year (printed attribution fact: the Imitation Game is 1950, and the human sign-off trim removed the spoken 'back to 1950', so the card is the only place the year appears). NO card or caption prints 1915 anywhere in this video.
parts.notes: right-anchored per human treatment decision; panel over screen is opaque

parts.direction: 'DETERMINISTIC' struck through in $accent on 'failed miserably', and under it a week counter lands: '1 week' 160px display (statMinFontPx) with '0 successes' under it in $muted. The strike is the scene's one accent.

Community dataset rows: three small rows land (LeRobot dataset tiles), each missing its 'success' column: the column header ticks to a dashed empty slot in $accent-soft. Label 'success labels: missing'.

'physics has its own mind': a hand-coded flowchart (if/then diamonds) on the left, on 'physics' an arrow bends off the chart by itself and draws its own squiggle to the right. Dashed 'can't hand-code this' chip.

Today's map: four numbered stops draw as a route, each landing on its spoken word: 1 deterministic policy (lands grey, gets struck), 2 what failed, 3 learning from data, 4 success. Route line in $rule, the one accent on stop 4. heroLeft.

Stop 5 'profiling my data' joins the route, chip 'what did I measure?' This is the handoff into the demo; the map leaves on 'let's get started' (demo begins at 'So here, if you can see my screen', cut 96.90).

Notebook ID card over the opening cells: the screen title OCRs to 'sim_pushTV2.ipynb', so the chip prints exactly that (spoken 'SIM Push-T V2, an ipynb notebook'). Below it a small Jupyter glyph ticks 'kernel attached' on 'attached to the appropriate kernel'. Import chip names 'gymnasium' as he says it. Right-anchored, opaque panel.

Punch-in on the notebook import cells: mark 'import gymnasium' and 'gym_pusht' as they are named. Chip 'no MuJoCo: Pymunk 2D' beside the mark, and the contrast lands here: a small 'MuJoCo' tile greyed out vs 'Pymunk' active (style: contrast over screen is opaque panel).
Punch-in on the env creation line: underline 'PushT-v0' and 'observation_type=state' as read. No marks drift (1.00-1.03 push) so a held still screen is never frozen.

'collect data instead of running a sim for a human observation': two tiny tiles, 'render for eyes' greyed with a slash vs 'collect frames' active in $accent (one accent). The data-engineering move at the top of the notebook: capture, don't watch.
Punch-in on the action space print from 'action space is the amount of area we allotted': a 5x5 grid draws over the output, x/y axes marked 0..5, one cell lights $accent on 'lowest ... highest'

Over the Push-T board: coordinate labels land as he reads them, pusher '390, 304' with a leader line to the pusher dot, outline '241.5, 268.5' at '3.3 degree angle', goal '0.78 degree radians' counting on screen. The Push-T task legend (pusher / block / outline) names each part once so the demo reads without the speaker.
Punch-in on 'n_episodes = 100': counter ticks '100 episodes' 160px on the number itself.
Seed diagram over the loop: three small boards, each with the pusher and block at a different spot, one $accent seed chip feeding them. 'each episode starts somewhere new'.

Punch-in on 'end less than 300' in the loop condition: a step meter fills, dashed ceiling labelled '300'; on 'whichever condition comes first, stop the loop' a second exit arrow 'done' lights above the ceiling.

'This is not a real policy': two tiny flow diagrams stacked. Top (the real one): read state -> decide action -> step. Bottom (his): sample(action_space) -> go, arrow skipping state with a dashed bypass. The bypass is the scene's accent. Lands as he defines what a policy means, closes on 'the random policy'.

Random policy scorecard: '0 / 100' successes lands 160px $ink, 'max coverage 0.115' under it in $muted with a tiny 11.5% fill bar (the bar is the scene's accent element). The one payoff of the random baseline.

'pure chaos does not create order': left, scattered dots in free motion labelled 'chaos' (the scene's accent: the scatter); right, the same dots refusing to form a T outline, dashed target ghost empty. The line is his: learning needs chaos, chaos alone builds nothing. Sets up why the random policy was still the right choice.

The hand-coded plan drawn: pusher dot bottom-left, star target top-right, an arrow draws 'go to star' then 'push in a straight line', a ghost outline shows the expected overlap. Dashed 'that should work' chip lands on 'That's what I thought. It should work, should happen.' The plan's own confidence makes the circling failure land; one accent (the arrow head).

The cowboy: on 'the unexpected happens' the board appears and the T starts circling (drawn from the real circling motion on screen); the line-art rope loop arcs over the spinning T, the pusher dot swings it in a loop on 'swinging it down in a loop'. Chip 'the cowboy policy'. The humanoid wears the series line-art cowboy hat here (human request 2026-11-12; costume for this beat only, the recurring robot stays hatless elsewhere). This beat is the video's comic beat: let the loop spin a full extra cycle past the last 'cowboy'.

Attempt 1 verdict: a 'was a failure' stamp lands on the spinning cowboy board, the rope dissolves; 'attempt 1: deterministic, failed' ledger row ticks under gZ9's ledger. Then 'hey, you know what? I am not super smart. Let me try AI.' lands as a small chip on 'try AI' (one accent: the stamp).
AI interlude: a terminal glyph types a prompt, then a small board: the pusher dot walks to a corner and sits, an X marks the spot. 'assumed the goal was 400x400' chip. One accent: the X.

'five minutes' vs 'a whole week': a clock glyph left, a 5-day strip of code/version chips right that fills on 'back and forth, bunch of codes, bunch of versions'. The week strip is $accent-soft, the clock hands $accent.

The thesis returns mid-demo as a mini quote card: 'to get a machine to learn ... you need some level of randomness in the learning process', attribution chip 'Dennis Noble / Alan Turing' (the names he credits on this line). Small card, right plate; the echo of g02 that tips him toward the diffusion policy.
Hugging Face promise: '64-65% success' count-up 160px, 'their eval' caption; on 'I did get a good chunk of successes' a small check ticks under the number.

First success replay: punch-in on the sim running the diffusion policy, the T block slides onto the outline; a 'success' tick lands in $accent on 'successfully pushes', chip 'that was settled' on 'settled'. The first green light after three failed attempts.
'80-90 min for 50 episodes' 160px with a small M5 Pro chip glyph. Sets up gZ14's arithmetic and g24's wall.
His own eval: '36 / 50 = 74%' 160px count-up on '74 percent', the % the one accent. Spelled as spoken.

'I built a profiler': a small gauge/lens glyph over the dataset tile, two check rows land as he names them, 'outliers?' and 'is the data good?', then a 'tested on Push-T community ' tick, an 'ALOHA community' tick, and the beat line 'now: my own data' in $accent (one accent). The profiler enters as a character here, before its own demo.
Dataset card: push_t_sim, fps 10, features list scrolls as he reads it, a 'no video captured' chip dashed with the reason 'machine capacity'. LeRobot dataset chip lands on 'LeRobot dataset'.
Punch-in on the collection loop: underline 'ds.add_frame' as he says it, tiny frame-stack glyph filling once. Two seconds, then releases to the full screen.

Punch-in on the printed schema: mark the schema keys as they appear (episode index, frame index, timestamp, action, observation), chip 'LeRobot schema: it just follows it'. The convention is the point: he writes nothing, the format is already right.
Dataset size: '1,050 episodes' 160px, splits beneath on 'a thousand ... 50': '1,000 random' + '50 diffusion' as two tinted blocks of a stacked bar.
'~300k frames' count-up 160px beside a small frame-stack glyph; '1,000 x 300 steps' caption (the arithmetic he narrates: all the random ones ran the full 300).

Metadata vs data check: two stacked tiles 'metadata' and 'data' with a counter on each; on 'they match exactly' an = lights between them, on 'count of zero' a check stamp 'everything matches' lands. The data-engineering discipline beat: verify, don't assume.

Two datasets, one task card: left tile '1,000 random, all failures', right tile '50 diffusion, 36 successes'; on 'would skew my data' the left tile slides behind a split line. 'split by task' chip closes the beat.

Episode-length picture drawn over the real distribution plot: the random rows all pin at 300 (flat ceiling of bars, 'all ran to the cap'), the diffusion rows spread 50-300 with the early finishers $accent-soft and a marker at 250 'success sooner'. Drawn bars track the real histogram on screen.
'IQR = 161' count-up 160px; a whisker plot band lands under it marking the 139-300 outlier window on 'below 139 or above 300'.

Profiler checklist over the report: idle episodes, dead joints, null values, nan values, cameras: each row ticks in sequence as he clears them ('no dead joints no idle episodes', 'no null values no nan values', 'no cameras, I didn't record them'). Ticks $accent (one accent row: the last tick). The checklist is the profiler's argument.
'36 succeeded / 1,050' 160px with the reason line '$muted: 1,000 of them are random policies' landing on the explanation. The number that makes the low rate make sense.

'The profiler itself works' chip: same profiler, my own data; 'filter by task type' mini diagram (one queue splits by policy), 'summary written to file system' footer tick. The profiler earns its keep before the takeaways.
Takeaway lead-in: 'LLMs are just parrots?' A drawn parrot-on-perch silhouette (line art, series style) beside the Reddit-style thread glyph ('search: AI parrot / LLM star parrot'). Sets up gZ21.

Quote echo card (g02's voice returns): 'In biological intelligence, the cellular processes are stochastic. There is a certain level of randomness ...' attribution 'Dennis Noble'. Aside chip 22px $muted: 'not a biologist, no AP bio' (his own joke on this line).

The Turing half of the quote: 'to make a machine learn, especially learn in a real world, the learning process has to have a level of randomness, stochasticity built in' attribution 'Alan Turing'. The two quote cards together re-state the thesis at the moment his data proves it.

'exactly what LLM training tries to emulate': network glyph left, a corpus block (stacked lines) feeds it, 'learns patterns' ticks out right. The same diagram family as gZ21's right side, drawn plain here so gZ21's contrast reads.

Parrot vs pattern-learner: left, a parrot mirroring two author tiles (Hemingway, Emerson, spelled correctly, the transcript's Ernst/Hummingway mishears are not screen copy); right, the same tiles feeding a small network glyph that emits a NEW tile. On 'create something new out of it' the right side wins: the new tile lifts and the parrot dims to $muted. Chip: 'same for code'.
Takeaway one as a counted row: 'Stochastic training is not a bug' 44px with 'a model that can be wrong can be right' $muted under it. Rises on 'On the contrary'.

The AI-collapse aside as a quote card: 'AI downturn? AI collapse? The bubble may burst. AI is here to stay and only going to improve' with a small 'hopeful' signature line 'future of CS and robotics'. One accent: 'here to stay'. Lighter card weight than g22 (this is a mood beat, not an argument).

Takeaway two: 'policy = f(data)' lands 90px as the formula types itself (font: display 900), then 'garbage in, garbage out' stamps beneath on 'garbage and garbage out' (the spoken wording), $accent on 'garbage' once. Data-curation chip on 'curated clean ... indicative' (1272-1276).

'treat policy as a black box': an opaque rounded box, 'data' arrow in, 'action' arrow out, 'our life becomes easy' chip. The abstraction a data engineer gets to use. On 'falls into place' the arrows snap straight.
Takeaway three: '50 episodes = 90 min on an M5 Pro' 160px count, then a 1000/2000/100k stack grows on 'thousand ... two thousand ... 100k' and stops, unresolved: 'imagine'. The compute wall, drawn.

The misleading-names lesson: a dataset tile reads 'success_v2', the success metric under it counts to 0 (strike lands on the tile name), chip 'curated, many successes inside: naming misleads'. On face value: no. The profiler's reason to exist, one line.

Next episode preview as three route chips that light in turn as he names them: 'Spark box: transfer the sims' (CUDA cores chip), 'ALOHA / SO-101', 'teleop episodes'. Right-anchored, opaque panel (over the desk wall it is lightReinforced per zones).
The ask: 'know a way to filter datasets on Hugging Face? leave a comment', a comment bubble glyph lands on 'leave me a comment'. $accent bubble (one accent).

End card: five brand rows from brand.md (YouTube @snudurupati with channel name 'AI for the Working Data Engineer' above, blog nudurupati.co, github, linkedin, x @srnudurupati) rise in 0.4s apart on 'goodbye', hold to the last frame (+2.3s hold per style). Panel x96-680 above y660 (measured wall), one $accent rule under the first row. Per the human sign-off decision 2026-11-12 the video ends at 24:09.0 on the end card, two frames after 'you.' (no face-turn tail: the human asked not to wait for the turn).
